title: A longtime 7News reporter is signing off
author: John Waller
bullets: Kimberly Bookman ends her 12-year tenure at 7News, announcing her departure through a social media post.
Bookman began at 7News in 2014 after working in Manchester, Baltimore, Spartanburg, and Elmira.
Bookman plans to remain in the Boston area and expressed pride in training reporters and hosting a clothing drive.

title: Cambridge man dies after being pulled from waters off Martha’s Vineyard
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Kevin Foster, 55, of Cambridge, died after being pulled from water at Long Point Wildlife Refuge, Martha's Vineyard.
First responders, including lifeguards, rescued multiple swimmers from the water on July 31 in West Tisbury.
Long Point beaches were closed following the incident due to hazardous swimming conditions causing rough surf and undertows.

title: Drake Maye runs through scouting report of Patriots’ crowded receiver room
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye highlights the depth of the Patriots' receiver room, featuring seven wideouts competing for playtime.
Maye praises A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs for their playmaking abilities and contributions in the revamped offense.
Newcomer Mack Hollins and returning Kayshon Boutte are noted for their versatility and consistency on the field.

title: Why one MLB analyst labeled Red Sox trade for Adley Rutschman as a ‘wild overpay on the face of it’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Red Sox acquired catcher Adley Rutschman from the Orioles in exchange for Carlos Narváez and three prospects.
ESPN analyst Kiley McDaniel described the trade as a 'wild overpay,' expressing doubts about the players Boston gave up.
Boston's need to replace Curtis Mead, who was injured, contributed to their aggressive pursuit of Rutschman.

title: Davis Sedaris on Duolingo, death, and dressing like a priest
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: David Sedaris discusses his liberation from Duolingo addiction in his new essay collection, 'The Land and Its People'.
Sedaris expresses candid views on personal themes such as his father's death and his family's complex relationships.
Sedaris launches his 'Lobster Roll Tour' in New England, with stops planned in Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Vermont.

title: John C. Reilly jumped on stage to sing at a Boston dive bar
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: John C. Reilly performed at Tavern at the End of the World, a dive bar in Charlestown, near Somerville.
Reilly joined local band Bosstown Heavy on stage, singing '54-46 (That’s My Number)' by Toots and the Maytals.
Following the performance, Reilly visited Kelly’s Diner in Somerville for breakfast the next morning.

title: Mass. woman found after going missing for 27 hours in N.H. woods
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Megan Kelley, 39, from Fall River, went missing 27 hours from Dolly Copp Campground, NH before being found.
A hiking couple discovered Kelley on an access road near biking trails in Gorham, leading to her rescue.
Kelley was taken to Androscoggin Valley Hospital; officials unsure how she reached the location, no severe injuries reported.

title: Plymouth woman dies after tree falls on her porch
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: A 61-year-old Plymouth woman died after a tree fell on her porch during strong winds.
First responders tried life-saving measures before she was transported to a local hospital and pronounced dead.
Authorities are withholding her identity as they notify her family; the incident remains under investigation.

title: There’s a pig loose on Martha’s Vineyard, apparently
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: A pig is on the loose in Edgartown, Martha’s Vineyard, prompting a search by local police.
The pig was last seen on Chase Road, moving toward Dark Woods Road, according to police reports.
Residents are advised to contact Edgartown Animal Control at 508-939-1782 if they spot the animal.

title: Boston has one of the best wine bars, wine shops in America, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Gray's Hall in Boston ranked No. 10 in USA Today's list of best wine bars in America for 2026.
Neighborhood Wines in Boston is named No. 10 on USA Today's list of best wine shops in America.
USA Today's 2026 10Best Readers’ Choice Awards involves reader votes and expert-selected nominations across various categories.
